audit.whatIsWrong: The entry states twice that Counter Strike absorbs Tongue Lash: wants.foe[0] "Activate Counter Strike before you reach 3 stacks so the dodge absorbs your empowered Tongue Lash", and whys[1] "Jax hits Counter Strike and can now dodge your empowered Tongue Lash entirely".
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges non-turret BASIC ATTACKS only, and separately gives 25% reduced damage from champion AoE abilities. Tongue Lash is a single-target ability, so Counter Strike does nothing to it — not dodged, not even the 25% reduction. This is the most consequential error in the matchup because it inverts the correct play. As written, a Tahm Kench sees Counter Strike go up and stops trying to land his Q, which means he never reaches three An Acquired Taste stacks and never gets his stun. The truth is the reverse: Counter Strike is the window in which he should still be throwing Q, because it is the one part of his damage Jax's E cannot touch. He should only stop AUTO-attacking — and that is a separate reason, since each dodged attack raises Counter Strike's own stun damage by 20%, up to +100%.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks only. Stop autoing, keep landing Tongue Lash.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jax — E Counter Strike: 'dodge all incoming non-turret basic attacks', 'take 25% reduced damage from all area of effect abilities sourced from champions', 'damage increases by 20% for each attack dodged, up to a 100% increase'
champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q Tongue Lash damages 'the first unit hit' (single target ability, not a basic attack)

audit.whatIsWrong: The levels 4-5 stage is written as though Jax already has his ultimate: spikes[1] "Jax's R passive stacks are charging and he wins extended duels", mid "Jax's R passive is stacking between fights", whys[3] "Jax's R passive grants massive bonus armor and magic resist in duels".
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms is not available until level 6 — at levels 4-5 Jax has no ultimate at all. The entry has moved his level-6 spike two levels early, which makes the 4-5 window read as more dangerous than it is and hides the fact that this is one of the stretches where Tahm Kench is least outgunned. The attack-speed ramp the text is groping for is actually his PASSIVE, Relentless Assault, which the entry never names.
audit.corrected: No ultimate before 6. The 4-5 ramp is Relentless Assault (consecutive basic attacks increase attack speed).
sources: champ-data/_kits/jax.json — P Relentless Assault: 'Jax's consecutive basic attacks continuously increase his Attack Speed'; R Grandmaster-at-Arms is the ultimate slot

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] and wants.foe[2] both attribute Jax's bonus armour and magic resist to the PASSIVE half of Grandmaster-at-Arms ("his R passive grants massive bonus armor and magic resist in duels", "his R passive grants enough defensive stats to survive a Devour window").
audit.why: Wrong half of the ability, and the difference is a decision the player has to make in a real fight. The passive half is an attack stacking mechanic — up to 2 stacks, then an empowered basic attack dealing bonus magic damage. The resistances come from the ACTIVE, and they last 8 seconds. That makes them a timer to outlast, not a permanent stat block to give up against. Since Devour's hold plus Tahm Kench's own front-line durability is measured in the same handful of seconds, whether the resists are permanent or an 8-second button is precisely what decides if the Devour window is worth taking.
audit.corrected: The active grants the armour and MR, for 8 seconds. The passive is the third-attack magic damage.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jax — R active grants 'bonus armor... and bonus magic resistance equal to 60% of that amount' for 8 seconds; passive generates stacks on basic attacks up to 2, empowering the next attack

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "Counter Strike's cooldown is short enough that two trades in the same wave genuinely threaten your kill", and whys[3] repeats "his short Counter Strike cooldown".
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 seconds — at the levels being described it is rank 2 or 3, so 15 to 13 seconds. That is the LONGEST cooldown in Jax's laning kit by a wide margin (Leap Strike is 8 down to 6, Empower is 7 down to 3) and it is the single most punishable thing he has. Calling it short tells the player there is no window to punish, which removes the entire reason to bait it — and the full layer's own cooldown breakdown already says 'Bait it', so the two layers contradict each other.
audit.corrected: 17s at rank 1, 15s at rank 2. It is the window, not the reason there is no window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jax.json — E cooldown 17/15/13/11/9, Q 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, W 7/6/5/4/3; wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Jax confirms 17/15/13/11/9

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 plan is "Abyssal Voyage gives you a global escape and repositioning threat that removes his dive-and-kill angle... he cannot follow your R, so every successful roam punishes his passive split-focus nature" (mid), and "Abyssal Voyage online removes his kill-lane threat" (whys[4]).
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and is not on the live champion. Tahm Kench has no global and no escape ultimate. Against Jax this is doubly wrong: the entry promises the player he can disengage and roam away from a split-pushing duelist, when in fact his level 6 is Devour — a commitment tool that cannot even be cast on Jax below three An Acquired Taste stacks.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, gated at three stacks. There is no escape ultimate and no roam threat.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour; P 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'; no global in kit

audit.why: Two things the entry gets right and I left alone. 'Do not auto him through the dodge window or you hand him a free stun' is correct and is now better justified — each dodged attack scales Counter Strike's damage by 20%. And wants.you[1], 'swallowing him with Devour — he cannot auto or use E while inside you', is the right use of the ultimate against this specific champion.

55.2% over 904 games, and late explicitly cites 'the 55% win rate is earned entirely in this late window' — consistent with the packet and with the level chart handing Tahm Kench first item and 2+ items. No elo-tier language anywhere in the entry.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his window and you need to respect it — Jax's R passive is stacking between fights, his W adds on-hit magic damage to every extended trade, and Counter Strike's cooldown is short enough that two trades in the same wave genuinely threaten your kill. Play for CS, throw Tongue Lash to poke and maintain stack threat without fully committing, and activate Thick Skin to shield if he forces an all-in so the grey health doesn't bleed out. At level 6 the lane shifts: Abyssal Voyage gives you a global escape and repositioning threat that removes his dive-and-kill angle, and critically you can now roam and return to lane without losing the grey-health advantage Thick Skin built up — he cannot follow your R, so every successful roam punishes his passive split-focus nature.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his window and you need to respect it — Relentless Assault ramps his attack speed on every consecutive auto, his W adds on-hit magic damage to every extended trade, and Counter Strike sits at 15s on rank 2, so a baited one is a genuine gap. Play for CS, throw Tongue Lash to poke and maintain stack threat without fully committing, and activate Thick Skin to shield if he forces an all-in so the grey health doesn't bleed out. At level 6 the lane shifts: Devour comes online and at three An Acquired Taste stacks it removes him mid-combo, and critically Grandmaster-at-Arms only holds its bonus armour and magic resist for 8 seconds — outlast that timer instead of fighting into it, and answer his split pressure with wave control rather than a duel.

notes: The Counter Strike error is the most damaging single line I found across my whole slice, because it is not merely a wrong name — it tells the player to stop doing the one thing that works. Worth noting that the FULL layer already had it right ('Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it.') while the CONTENT layer had it backwards; the two layers are disagreeing on mechanics, not just on wording, which suggests they were generated independently and never cross-checked. That is the same pattern as the level-chart contradictions I have flagged in gwen, heimerdinger, illaoi and irelia, and it may be worth a systematic layer-vs-layer consistency pass rather than per-matchup fixes. This is also the only matchup in my slice where I went to the web: the kit files genuinely cannot answer 'does Counter Strike dodge abilities', since that is exactly the class of fact the empty needsResearch block covers. League Wiki confirmed basic-attacks-only plus the 25% AoE reduction, and confirmed the 17/15/13/11/9 cooldown and that the R resistances are on the active for 8s.
